summary: SSH gateway SSO key derivation mismatch after Okta group sync failure causing CLI auth 403 for new hires
description:
Issue summary:
New hires (onboarding cohort 2026-03) report 403 errors when attempting to authenticate to the SSH gateway via SSO-enabled CLI (redwood-ssh). The web console SSO works for affected users; the failure is limited to CLI/SSH gateway flows.

Impact:
- 7 new engineers unable to access internal bastion hosts for dev/debugging starting 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC.
- Blocked onboarding tasks and increased time-to-productivity; one PagerDuty rotation delayed.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (ssh-gateway cluster v2.1.4)
- Okta directory: OKTA-prod tenant (group sync job runs every 5m)
- Affected clients: redwood-ssh CLI v1.3.2 on macOS and linux.

Steps to reproduce:
1) New user completes Okta SSO onboarding, is placed into groups via SCIM rule.
2) User runs `redwood-ssh login` to retrieve SSO-derived SSH key.
3) CLI returns HTTP 403 with body: "permission denied: key derivation mismatch".
4) Web SSO and console access succeed for same user.

Observed logs / traces:
- ssh-gateway logs (2026-03-10 09:16 UTC): "key-derive: user=linatest@example.com derivation_checksum=0x9f2a expected=0x65b1"
- Okta sync service logs: several 504s to /groups endpoint between 09:10-09:14 UTC; last successful full sync at 09:04 UTC.
- redwood-ssh client trace: received 403 with error_code=SSO_KEY_MISMATCH.

Hypothesis:
- Partial/failing Okta group sync left user in an intermediate state where user profile attributes required for deterministic SSH key derivation (okta:externalId + groupHash) were inconsistent between identity-provisioning service and ssh-gateway. The gateway uses a derivation function that relies on canonicalized group list; if group sync truncates, checksum mismatch occurs and gateway rejects derived key.

Temporary mitigation attempted:
- Manual re-run of full SCIM sync (okta-sync job) for affected users; 5/7 users regained access after sync completion at 09:22 UTC.
- For remaining 2 users we temporarily generated and uploaded service-account SSH keys via identity-provisioning console as a stopgap.

Scope and next steps planned:
- Priority: investigate root cause of Okta group sync 504 spikes and harden retry/backoff.
- Validate derivation algorithm tolerates partial group lists or add defensive fallback comparing canonicalized partial checksums with allowances for recent sync windows.
- Create an automated reconciliation job that detects checksum mismatches and enqueues a re-sync for affected users.
- Audit recent deploys to identity-provisioning and ssh-gateway for incompatible changes to canonicalization.

Supporting artifacts and pointers:
- Relevant infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123
- SRE runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/SSH+Gateway+Runbook
- Slack thread: #support (link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01SUPPORT/p1700000000000000)
comments: Lina Chen - 2026-03-10: Reported issue after running onboarding checklist. Attached client logs and timestamped errors. Noted that web console SSO is fine. Marked P1 because multiple new hires blocked.
Support (Jasper Mills) - 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Started triage and requested full OKTA sync logs and ssh-gateway debug output. Assigned to SRE on-call for deeper investigation.

SRE (Mariam Ortega) - 2026-03-10: Observed repeated 504s hitting Okta /api/v1/groups during the 09:10-09:14 window. Re-ran full SCIM sync; most users recovered. Collecting gateway traces and comparing checksum inputs.

Identity Team (Tomás Rivera) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed no recent schema changes to group attribute mapping. Investigating transient network errors to Okta at 09:10; found increased latency on one hop to okta-prod-east. Backfilled a fix to the sync job to increase timeout and add exponential backoff. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123

SRE (Mariam Ortega) - 2026-03-11: Found derivation function normalizes group list by timestamp order. If sync is partial, canonical ordering differs causing checksum mismatch. Proposing small gateway change to accept key if checksum matches last-known-good within 5m window OR automatically trigger on-demand re-sync for user.

Jasper Mills - 2026-03-12: Implemented emergency reconciliation script to identify recent SSO_KEY_MISMATCH events and enqueue SCIM re-sync per user. Applied to affected cohort; remaining two users recovered. Rolling out fix branch to staging for gateway fallback logic. Filing follow-up task to harden monitoring and add alert for Okta sync failure rate > 3 in 5m.
